body:
## Summary
Every scripted interaction in the guided walk becomes a declared DOOR - the anchor(s) to click, the board effect that proves it worked, and the checked API call that does the same work - run by one engine primitive. A click that lands but changes nothing is reported, the fallback is checked, and the walk only narrates what the board shows.

## Description
The demo's whole claim is that it drives the real product with real clicks (simWalkSteps.ts:293-301). Today a click is judged by one bit - was the element found - and two of the four clicks broke inside a week without any gate or log noticing: since 2026-09-16 the Publish button opens a terms dialog (JobsDraftsPanel.tsx:176-199), so the click 'succeeds', no fallback runs, and the walk sources zero candidates and walks on (useSimulationWalk.ts:271-294); since 2026-09-17 offer rows hide the quick-accept (LedgerCells.tsx:97-100), so the climactic Send-offer click falls back to the API on every run after a 9 s wait - through the no-deadline door the product itself closed. Four more writes are unchecked (useSimulationWalk.ts:463, 488, 522, 554), and the run declares 'Hired' without reading the stage. The seam: `clickEl -> boolean` plus four hand-written fallbacks. The move: `SIM_DOORS` (pure, in simDoor.ts) declares per door the click path (including a confirm/open step), the effect predicate over the board, and the API equivalent; `door()` in the engine runs click -> bounded effect wait -> checked API fallback -> effect re-check, and records `{route, reason}` per chapter in SimState. The two dead doors are repaired by adding the missing anchors on the product side (publish-confirm on the dialog, decide on the ledger's third door) so the real flows - terms dialog, deadline lever - are what the viewer watches.

## Flow
1. Write simDoor.test.ts: doorOutcome cases, SIM_DOORS anchor source-scans, the no-bare-POST scan of useSimulationWalk.ts, hiredEffect. Watch them fail.
2. simDoor.ts: SimDoor type, SIM_DOORS (publish, confirmSlot, offerSend, offerAccept), doorOutcome, hiredEffect - pure.
3. useSimulationEngine.ts: `door(doorId, ids)` over clickEl/waitEntry/okJson.
4. useSimulationWalk.ts: the four click sites and the four unchecked writes go through door()/okJson; done:true gated on hiredEffect; per-chapter route recorded.
5. Add data-sim-click="publish-confirm" (JobsPublishDialog.tsx confirm) and data-sim-click="decide" (LedgerCells.tsx third door).
6. Catalog keys for the new reasons (log.doorNoEffect, error.doorNoEffect) in four locales; update docs/features/simulation/README.md (the 'API fallback is labelled' gap becomes 'verified').

## Expected impact
The demo sources a real pool again and shows the real Send-offer modal with its deadline; a click whose door changes semantics is named in the run log on the next run instead of silently degrading the tour; no chapter narrates an outcome the server refused. Closes the class 'a UI change breaks the tour without a red anything' at the one seam every chapter shares.

## Evaluation
Claim: every scripted walk interaction is verified by its board effect and every walk write is checked.
Before: 0 of 8 acceptance cases pass
After: 8 of 8
Method: npm run test:unit (simDoor.test.ts, simWalkSteps.test.ts), then the overlay's integration gate
Result: pending build
Gate: contract

title: Resume a reloaded walk at the chapter the board shows, not Reset and restart
acceptance: resumePointOf({entries: [], axis: DEFAULT_STAGE_AXIS}) -> null (nothing to resume; Start stays the action)
entries of a job whose jobTitle is not isSimTitle() are ignored: a real candidate at the offer stage never becomes a resume target
a (SIM) job whose entries all sit on the entry-role stage -> {phase:'match', jobId}
a (SIM) job with entries on screenedLandingStage(axis) and no approval -> {phase:'screen', targetId: the compareByMatchScoreDesc-first screened entry, targetLabel}

target one stage past screened with approvalKind 'calendar' -> {phase:'interview'}; target on the offer-role stage with approvalKind 'offer_review' -> {phase:'offer'}; offer-role stage with approvalKind null -> {phase:'hired'}
target on the terminal-role stage -> null with reason 'complete' (a finished run offers Reset, not Resume)
chaptersFrom('offer') -> the ids ['offer','hired'] in SIM_CHAPTERS order; chaptersFrom on an id not in SIM_CHAPTERS throws

POST /api/sim/reset {hold:true, keep:true} claims the lease, answers a token and purges nothing (no `cleared`, simResidue unchanged); refused SIM_RUN_ACTIVE 409 while another token holds the workspace

app/features/shell/simulation/useSimulationWalk.ts:204-207 - every run starts with POST /api/sim/reset {hold:true}, and app/api/sim/reset/route.ts:106-111 purges every (SIM) row on that claim - so the only way back into a walk is to destroy it
app/features/shell/simulation/SimulationProvider.tsx:98-101 - pagehide releases the tab's lease, so after a reload the board keeps the walk's rows but no tab owns them

app/features/shell/simulation/simRunControl.ts:71-78 - consoleMode shows the sim console when residue > 0, and the console's actions are Start (purges) or Reset (purges) - SimControlDockSimFace.tsx:60-66 renders only startSim when not running and not done

app/features/shell/simulation/useSimulationEngine.ts:57-69 - getBoard already returns the workspace's entries (jobId, jobTitle, stage, approvalKind, matchScore per BOARD_ENTRY_FIELDS, app/_lib/db/pipeline.ts:117-140) AND its stage axis, so a resume point is derivable from one read with no new storage
app/features/shell/simulation/constants.ts:21-23 - isSimTitle() is the single-sourced test for a walk's own rows
docs/features/simulation/README.md:295-296 - 'The seven SIM_PHASES are a fixed script ... no way to replay one phase without a full reset'
rollback: The route change is additive (a new `keep` flag; absent it, every existing shape behaves byte-identically and reset-route.test.ts pins that), and the walk's `from` parameter defaults to the first chapter. Reverting the series removes the Resume action and the flag; no data or schema is touched.
runner_up: Step mode holds the overlay moments: the screen-wave audit, the group evaluation and the candidate's offer page auto-dismiss on a timer INSIDE the chapter action (useSimulationWalk.ts:414-415, 506-507, 556-557) before the presenter's gate at :141, so the presenter can never talk over the Art. 22 audit - hold them until Next in step mode.
body:
## Summary
Adopts the open escalated item 'Resume a live walk after reload from the held lease' (leftover-develop-2026-09-17, M, risk 4, architecture, not drained). A reload, a crashed tab or a presenter who navigated away mid-demo gets a 'Resume at Offer - <candidate>' action that re-enters the walk at the chapter the board proves it reached, instead of Reset-and-replay-seven-chapters.

## Description
The walk's progress already lives on the server - the (SIM) job and its entries survive a reload - but the walk can only begin at chapter one, and chapter one's first act is a purge (useSimulationWalk.ts:204-207, route.ts:106-111). So the console, which correctly surfaces the residue (simRunControl.ts:71-78), offers only the two buttons that delete it. The guided-tours standard's lifecycle rule is the opposite: progress persists and resume is the default, and resume re-validates and replays the activation path rather than repainting saved state. The board IS the validated record: `resumePointOf(board, axis)` (pure) finds the (SIM) job, the followed candidate and the first chapter whose postcondition the board does not yet satisfy, all resolved by stage ROLE from the live axis the way the walk already does (useSimulationWalk.ts:218-221). The route gains a no-purge claim (`{hold:true, keep:true}`) so resuming takes the lease without wiping the run it resumes; run(from) seeds jobId/targetId/targetLabel from the resume point (offerToken via the existing /api/sim/offer-link) and walks `chaptersFrom(phase)`.

## Flow
1. simWalkResume.test.ts: the resume-point, chaptersFrom and keep-claim cases; watch them fail.
2. simWalkResume.ts: resumePointOf + chaptersFrom, pure over PipelineEntryView[] + StageDef[].
3. route.ts + simRunLease.ts: `keep` on the hold claim skips resetSim; claimInit(lease, {keep}) helper; route test pins old shapes unchanged.
4. useSimulationWalk.ts: run(from?) skips completed chapters, seeds the context, logs log.resumed.
5. SimulationProvider.tsx + types: on console mount with residue and no live foreign lease, read the board once and expose `resumable` + `resume()`.
6. SimControlDockSimFace.tsx: Resume at <phase> as the primary action beside Reset when resumable.
7. Four-locale keys; README known gap rewritten.

## Expected impact
A mid-demo reload costs one click instead of a purge and a 2-3 minute replay (SIM_RUN_TTL_MS comment, sim-store.ts: 'A full walk is ~2-3 minutes of beats'); a public demo visitor who refreshes lands back where they were. It also turns the documented 'no way to replay one phase' gap into a derived entry point that the open 'start from one SIM_PHASE' item can reuse.

## Evaluation
Claim: a reloaded walk re-enters at the chapter its board state proves it reached, without purging.
Before: 0 of 8 acceptance cases pass
After: 8 of 8
Method: npm run test:unit (simWalkResume.test.ts, reset-route.test.ts), then the overlay's integration gate
Result: pending build
Gate: architecture
